newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican generals named to head two airports.
newsitem.headline: Mexican generals named to head two airports.

text.p: Army generals will take over the administration of airports in two major Mexican cities after police recently discovered the airports had been used by drug traffickers, officials said on Saturday.

A statement by the government-run Airport Services said Brigadier Gens. Alejandro Martinez Belmont and Alberto Trejo Garcia will take over operations at the airports of Toluca, some 38 miles (60 km) west of Mexico City, and Cuernavaca, about 50 miles (80 km) south of the capital, respectively.

The heads of those airports were replaced after Mexican police arrested more than 25 people earlier this month at a drug lord's family wedding. Police said many of the guests had been flown to the wedding from airports in Toluca and Cuernavaca.

The Attorney General's office said three planes owned by Juarez drug cartel chief Amado Carillo Fuentes took off from Toluca and picked up guests at Cuernavaca before flying to northern Sinaloa state for the wedding of Carillo's sister.

Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo has increasingly relied on the military to take a high-profile role in the drug war and to crack down on crime. Army generals now head Mexico City's police force and the country's top anti-drug agency.
Some two-thirds of the cocaine that enters the United States comes through Mexico from South America, officials say.
